newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Jan jobless "well over" 4.4 mln - union head.
newsitem.headline: German Jan jobless "well over" 4.4 mln - union head.

text.p: The deputy head of Germany's DGB Trade Union Federation said on Monday she expected the country's jobless total to rise to substantially above 4.4 million in January compared to December's 4.15 million.

"I expect it well over 4.4 million in January and then in February it can be over 4.5 million," Ursula Engelen-Kefer said in a telephone interview. Engelen-Kefer also sits on the board of the German Labour Office, which publishes the monthly unemployment data.

Bernhard Jagoda, head of the Nuremberg-based Labour Office, said after the publication of December's figures that the 4.5 million figure could be reached if the poor weather experienced so far this winter continued up until March.

Engelen-Kefer said that with Germany's current modest economic growth rate, and assuming that no direct measures were taken to ease unemployment, she thought the country's jobless total would average 4.2 million for the 1997 year.

She renewed earlier demands from the DGB and a number of separate union bodies in Germany for a reduction in the amount of overtime worked and a shorter working week. She also insisted job-creating public infrastructure projects be accelerated.

DGB chairman Dieter Schulte said at a news conference in Bonn earlier on Monday that such measures were necessary this year if the government's stated goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000 was to be achieved.
